text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — we're seeing a spike of TLS handshakes failing from ap-southeast-1 -> edge-proxy this morning. Errors show KMS decrypt denied in the proxy sidecar. Anyone touched keystore RBAC overnight?

Alex Rivera: Not me. Which key? any logs?

Maria Chen: Logs pasted below (redacted):
```
proxy-sidecar[pid=2145]: mTLS handshake failed: client cert verify failed: KMS decrypt error: PERMISSION_DENIED
proxy-sidecar[pid=2145]: key_version: projects/redwood-prod/locations/ap-southeast1/keyRings/edge/cryptoKeys/proxy-cert/cryptoKeyVersions/3
```

Sanjay Patel: I merged a change to the keystore roles last night — tightened who can call `cloudkms.cryptoKeys.decrypt`. The PR was to scope service-account access per-region (was global). I tagged it in #eng-iam. Might be hitting proxies using the old global SA.

Emily Sec: Oh — that would explain it. Are proxies using regional SA annotations or the global one? We recently advised apps to switch to workload identity; some sidecars still mount the legacy SA via node pool annotation.

Jordan Lee: Confirmed: ap-southeast-1 proxy pods still have `redwood-proxy-global-sa@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com` in the node metadata. The new policy removed decrypt from that global SA but gave decrypt to `redwood-proxy-ap-southeast1@...` in region.

Maria Chen: That mismatch would produce PERMISSION_DENIED on KMS decrypt calls. Quick mitigation options?

Sanjay Patel: Short-term: add decrypt to the global SA again (fast rollback) or patch the proxy pods to use the regional SA. I'm +1 on rollback for immediate recovery, then we do a staged migration.

Emily Sec: Agreed. Also we need to backfill audit logs and detect any requests that failed silently. Query for KMS decrypt denies with this filter (GCP):
```
logName="projects/redwood-prod/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Fdata_access"
protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"
protoPayload.status.code=7  # PERMISSION_DENIED
resource.labels.location="ap-southeast1"
```

Jordan Lee: I ran that and got ~1200 denied decrypt attempts in the last 30m, mostly from `proxy-sidecar` instances across three clusters. Some upstream services switched to cached certs and are OK, others retried and failed.

Maria Chen: OK let's do the rollback + audit plan. Action items: 1) Sanjay to rollback the RBAC change (re-add decrypt to global SA) and open a follow-up PR to migrate proxies. 2) Jordan to run the audit query and dump a CSV of failed reqs to the incident ticket. 3) Emily to add an alert for KMS PERMISSION_DENIED spikes in ap-southeast1 and add runbook links. 4) Maria to coordinate rollout/announcement to infra teams.

Sanjay Patel: I'm on the rollback now. Command I'll run (GCP IAM):
```
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod \
  --member=serviceAccount:redwood-proxy-global-sa@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
I'll also tag the change with `#rollback` and roll forward with a canary for ap-southeast1 only.

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered by @Sanjay Patel -> iam/keystore-policy (change: add role back). CI checks: passed.

Sanjay Patel: Rolled back. Confirmed policy binding exists again. Please monitor.

Jordan Lee: After rollback, denied decrypts dropped to ~2/min and most handshakes recovered within 90s. I'll export the full list to the incident ticket (INC-2026-118).

Emily Sec: Filing two follow-ups: (1) enforcement plan to prevent region drift — we should add a pre-merge CI check that inspects service account usage across clusters. (2) Add a KMS permission-monitor alert with a 5-min burn rate threshold. I'll create cards.

Maria Chen: Good. One more postmortem note: the failure surface was amplified because some proxies don't cache certs long enough — we should extend cert TTL for edge proxies to tolerate short KMS outages (config = `proxy.cert_cache_ttl`). Jordan, can you open a config PR?

Jordan Lee: Will do. PR linking to this thread.

Emily Sec: Also adding a runbook snippet for future similar incidents: if KMS decrypt denies spike -> check SA bindings -> check node/Pod SA annotations -> rollback policy or patch pods.

Maria Chen: Thanks all. Closing the active incident window — monitoring for 2 hours. Assigning follow-up owners in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
